requirements.notes: Sections 2.1-2.8: today's table cited (DEUS_Levels.js:994-1016), the property set, natural materials with kg per 2-ft voxel, SRD AC/HP link and spans; new loose materials (rubble, loose_fill, sediment, ash, ice, scrap, mineral_trace, broken_timber, dust; snow reserved) and assemblies with free ids 6-37; the exact loose record; input to PROPOSED-Q-01. DT values and most HP values are marked extrapolated (OQ-Q-10). Fix 1: one kg rounding rule (nearest integer, halves up, once) stated in section 2.3; timber_floor 121, timber_roof 139 and conjured_stone 389 kg per voxel now follow it; floating-ice capacity is the integer floor(7 h^2 / 2) with h = 61 cm per stratum (13,023 and 52,094 kg).

Sections 3.1-3.6: element-by-element table (walls, floors, roofs, doors, windows, stairs, ramps, columns, bridges, furniture, conjured walls), thickness in 2-ft slices, the build job writing strata through setStrata with the constructed flag (DEUS_Levels.js:1602), foundations as reusable strata (SET-4), save and object migration, catalogue slot names only (DEC-011, DEC-007).

Sections 4.1-4.6: members, bearing and lateral support to the world floor at zMin, span table derived from cantilever bending with S_MAX 12, load and capacity with HP bands, natural rock and ledges (V128), vertical propagation across -16..+15. The natural-rock bound is the design default while DEC-010 is OPEN (OQ-Q-01).

Sections 5.1-5.7: triggers (levels:strataChanged at DEUS_Levels.js:1558 and load events with band throttling), one FIFO queue with SUPPORT_BUDGET 256, local evaluation, lazy per-chunk records, worst-case bound table with arithmetic, determinism, area edges and LOD (proposes an amendment to PROPOSED ADR-003 section 16.5).

Sections 6.1-6.6: failing state and warnings, the cascade through layers, equal-mass conversion to loose debris, talus by angle of repose with a budget, SRD falling (1d6 per 10 ft) and Earthquake collapse (5d6, burial DC 20) as the damage baseline with an extrapolated addition (OQ-Q-08), and the recheck the rubble triggers. Fix 1: one fall-length rule (section 6.2 step 3): a unit's fall is dropTop = e1 - landing strata (the drop of the surface it stood on), so one layer is 10 ft and 1d6; dropGap = e0 - (landing + 1) is the debris's air gap and feeds only the debris addition; section 6.5, T10 and the collapse:impact payload use the same rule.

Sections 7.1-7.6 state the Lane Q side of the contract with Lane R (C1-C9: HP-only writes through the strata writer, capacityThresholdsHP band crossings, Collapse.breakElement as the one HP-0 path, events back, mass, roofs before walls by the support rule, foundations, time domains), an abandoned-house walk-through ending as rubble, and the D-1 duration table. Lane R pushed its side (origin/task/lane-r 6613418f, R-05, unreviewed) before this design was finished; ownership agrees, and the naming differences are resolved in section 9.7 by adopting Lane R's names. Both sides are unreviewed.

Sections 8.1-8.8: existing applyVolumeDamage cited with its gaps (SUP-5), the PROPOSED ADR-003 section 18.2 rule adopted with half-feet geometry (10-ft layers, 2-ft slices), the pass and resist tables per material and damage type (ADR Q18), SRD area versus physical remainder for units on both layers, worked numbers, breaching and debris, coupling to GP.07.02, DEC-022 and SIM.60 primitives, cost. Table values are extrapolated (OQ-Q-10).

Sections 9.1-9.7: families, forms and units; ledger entries for 19 paths including build, dig, mine, quarry, collapse, blast, rubble clearing, salvage and conjured matter; how each LAND-1 leak closes with the mutant that catches it; conjured matter as a logged source/sink (DEC-018 PM default, not answered); checks; no ore creation (LIFE-002). PARTIAL because the ledger unit and family list are not reconciled across the sibling lanes: Lane Q uses kg, Lane R 1/16 lb, Lane W grams (section 9.7); raised in escalation.md for the PM. Fix 1: lava solidifies at 2 du (2,053 kg each) per basalt voxel of 4,106 kg, basalt's one kgPerVoxel; an odd last du becomes basalt-lineage loose rubble (section 9.1, section 9.2 row 18).

Sections 10.1-10.5: every structure with its sparse representation, size and whether it is saved; memory per building, region and layer at 32 layers with arithmetic; save size; CPU per tick with budgets and position in the tick; LOD regions and a batched deep-history ruin reduction. All figures are arithmetic, not measured.

Sections 11.1-11.3: 11 emitted events with payloads and in-tick order, APIs (Support.query, wouldSupport, digRisk, enqueue, Collapse.trigger, Volume.damage, Loose.*, Ledger.*), and per-consumer contracts for SIM.40.02, SIM.40.03, SIM.40.04, SIM.50.10, SIM.50.02 (D-4 dependency flagged), SIM.50.05, SIM.60, GP.07.02 and Lane W.

Sections 12.1-12.3: 18 automatable tests (T1-T18) including the deterministic cave-in, towers across +1..+4 and +4..+15, blasts breaching one and two floors, exact ledger totals per path, zero full-world scans, each with at least one mutant that must fail, run at the 9-layer and 32-layer ranges; fixture list for SIM.40.04.

Section 13: eight PROPOSED-Q packages with real dependency IDs and tests, the dependency changes the audit section 6 asks for, notes for the PM and ADR owner, and the rulings the design depends on (D-1 open, D-4 and D-6 flagged). Owner questions are in the '## Owner questions' section (OQ-Q-01..14) and in ownerQuestions below.

proposedPackages.title: Material and structure model: property table as catalogue data, ids 6-37, loose record, object and item kg, compositions, load-time validator
acceptanceTests: Validator rejects a material missing any section 2.2 property; mutant: remove spanBase from one id, the validator must exit 1
Loose kg exact over 1,000 random deposits and takes; mutant: store loose mass as a 1/255 fill fraction, the exactness check must fail
T12 no ore: mutant rust -> iron ore row must fail

proposedPackages.title: Constructions as constructed strata (LAND-5, SUP-2, SET-4): build jobs write strata, balanced build masses, foundations and re-founding, save migration, removal of the isRoofed roof-deck side effect
acceptanceTests: T14 save migration; mutant: migration forgets the rubble object's mass
A built floor over a room is supported only through built walls; mutant: the build job places an object again, the floor must be reported unsupported
T5 build row: ledger balances; mutant: 1 kg leaked in the build transform

proposedPackages.title: Mass-conserving earthworks (LAND-1): mine, dig, quarry, dismantle, rubble clearing, salvage, spoil, rebuild from rubble
acceptanceTests: T5 rows for mine, dig, quarry, dismantle, clearing, salvage, rebuild; mutants: mining yields 2 stone with no spoil; dig drops a free stone 1 in 4; rubble pick yields 2 stone; roof-deck side effect restored

proposedPackages.title: Support evaluation and localized recheck: members, records, queue, failing set, warnings, Support.query / wouldSupport / digRisk
acceptanceTests: T1 deterministic cave-in; mutant: levels:strataChanged not enqueued
T6 zero full-world scans; mutant: per-tick sweep over all chunks
T7 local bound; mutant: S_MAX uncapped
T18 warning and rescue; mutant: failTick ignored

proposedPackages.title: Volume damage with attenuation: ADR-003 section 18 rule plus this design's pass/resist tables, breach order, SRD area versus remainder, ignition, debris
acceptanceTests: T3 blast breaches one floor; mutant: attenuation removed (all passPm 1000)
T4 blast breaches two floors; mutants: breach order reversed; 1-ft stratum height
T13 SRD numbers unchanged (with SIM.60.04); mutant: physics adds damage to creatures inside the SRD area

proposedPackages.title: Stable terrain at generation: extend the floating-rock pass to spans
acceptanceTests: T8 a fresh world has zero failing members at both ranges; mutant: the stability pass skipped

proposedPackages.title: Falls, impacts and burial for units and objects (V95, SUP-4)
acceptanceTests: T10 falls and burial: units on one-stratum floors at S0 of +1, +2 and +3 fall dropTop = 5, 10, 15 strata (10, 20, 30 ft) and take 1d6, 2d6, 3d6; mutants: the unit's fall measured as the air gap dropGap (0, 1, 2 dice); 1-ft stratum height (0, 1, 1 dice); burial not applied

proposedPackages.title: Support observability (AGENTS.md Rule 14): UF_Look and UF_Sheet explain why a member is supported or failing
acceptanceTests: Support.query matches a fresh evaluation after every mutation in the T1 fixture; mutant: a stale record kept after a dig

ownerQuestions.question: DEC-010 is OPEN: how far may natural rock reach sideways from a support?
options: (a) recommended: bounded by the material and thickness span table, keeping rechecks local (V133)
(b) unbounded lateral connectivity as the generator does, which needs a whole-area connectivity search after every dig
(c) DEC-010 option 2: full vertical support, no overhangs

ownerQuestions.question: How strong should materials be?
options: (a) recommended: the physically derived table
(b) the same table with every span doubled
(c) one span per material class (rock, soil, timber, masonry)

ownerQuestions.question: How realistic should constructed spans be (proposed: timber floors and roofs clear 20 ft, stone vaults 30 ft, bridge piers every 20 ft)?
options: (a) recommended: as proposed
(b) more generous (timber 30 ft, vaults 50 ft)
(c) stricter (timber 15 ft)

ownerQuestions.question: Does furniture carry load?
options: (a) recommended: furniture is load only, never support
(b) heavy furniture can prop a ceiling like a post
(c) furniture is neither load nor support

ownerQuestions.question: Do units' weights load floors?
options: (a) recommended: no, except Huge and Gargantuan creatures
(b) every unit is load
(c) no unit is load

ownerQuestions.question: Item masses and build costs, given that a 5-ft masonry wall cell weighs about 3.9 t with exact mass
options: (a) realistic masses: more, heavier building items
(b) abstract load units: today's item counts, with item kg set so each recipe balances exactly
(c) a middle scale

ownerQuestions.question: Where does mining spoil go (a mined voxel's mass beyond the stone items)?
options: (a) left as loose rubble at the work cell, to be hauled
(b) moved to a designated spoil heap as part of the job
(c) all of it yields as items

ownerQuestions.question: Collapse damage to creatures
options: (a) recommended: SRD Earthquake numbers (Dex save, 5d6, burial DC 20) plus +1d6 per further 10 ft the debris fell (dropGap), cap 20d6
(b) the SRD numbers alone
(c) damage scaled only by debris mass and height

ownerQuestions.question: Warning before a structure falls
options: (a) recommended: short creaks by material (timber 20 ticks, masonry 5, rock 0-10), none after a blast
(b) no warning ever
(c) long warnings (several game hours)

ownerQuestions.question: Blast feel: damage thresholds (SRD gives the rule, no numbers), the pass table, and whether 'spreads around corners' spells spread physical energy around corners
options: (a) recommended: the proposed tables with around-corners propagation where the SRD text says so
(b) the same tables, straight lines only (ADR-003 rule)
(c) tune both on the SIM.60.04 fixtures with the Owner

ownerQuestions.question: Roof decks that old saves got for free (DEUS_Floors.js:276)
options: (a) keep them with a logged one-time migration source
(b) remove them on load
(c) convert them to items on the floor below

ownerQuestions.question: Soil cannot span without depth: a soil tunnel with less than 20 ft of cover falls in unless propped
options: (a) accept: props become a real mining task (SIM.40.03)
(b) give soil a 1-cell span at any thickness
(c) soil tunnels never fall

ownerQuestions.question: Generated terrain that exceeds the spans
options: (a) the generator adds natural pillars
(b) the generator thins or removes the overhang
(c) generated terrain is exempt until something nearby changes

ownerQuestions.question: Walls fill a whole 5-ft cell, with thin walls expressed by their mass
options: (a) recommended: whole cells, as wall objects block a cell today
(b) walls on the edges between cells, a new geometry and a much larger change
